summary: Jörg Plassen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has held professorships at Geumgang University and Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).

Jörundur Garðar Hilmarsson was a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Oslo, the Sorbonne, and Leiden University, and under Werner Winter. He later taught at the University of Iceland from circa 1986 to 1992.

Jørn Borup was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Aarhus University (circa 1998–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and served there as an associate professor from circa 2006 to 2023.

Júlia Szivák works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Corvinus University, Eötvös Loránd University, Central European University, and Birmingham City University. Her academic posts include research associate at Eötvös Loránd University (2015) and Leverhulme Early Career Research Fellow at Nottingham.

Indologist Jürgen Hanneder studied at Munich, Bochum, Bonn, and Marburg, completing his PhD under Michael Hahn. After positions at Bonn and Halle-Wittenberg, he succeeded Hahn as professor at Marburg in 2007 and joined the Mainz Academy in 2021.
Jürgen Neuß works in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Harry Falk and completed his doctoral degree at the Free University of Berlin in 2007.

Jürgen Renn works in history, archaeology, and philosophy, earning his PhD from TU Berlin in 1987. He served as Director at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science from 1994 and became Director of the MPI of Geoanthropology in 2022.

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri was a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He served at Annamalai University, the University of Mysore, and as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Madras (circa 1929–1946).

K. A. Subramania Iyer worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, studying under Sylvain Lévi and Lionel David Barnett. He was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (1921–1960), Principal of Sanskrit College (1950–1951), and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
K. Ammini Amma is an Indologist who was a research student at the University of Madras, attested in 1940 and 1971.
K. Balasubramania Iyer was an Indologist who served as Managing Editor of the Journal of Oriental Research and was attested as Secretary at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute in 1945.
K. Jayakumar is an Indologist and linguist who studied at St. Joseph's Higher Secondary School, Thiruvananthapuram. He served in the Indian Administrative Service from circa 1978 to 2012.
K. Kanapathypillai was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Hartley College and the University of London from circa 1933 to 1936.

K. Kunjunni Raja was an Indologist and linguist who earned doctorates from Madras and London. He was Professor and Head of Sanskrit at the University of Madras from 1951 and later served at the Adyar Library and Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

K. L. Dhammajoti is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kelaniya under Yinshun and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. He held posts at Kelaniya, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hong Kong.

K. Madhava Krishna Sarma was an Indologist who studied as a research student under C. Kunhan Raja. He was affiliated with the Adyar Library and Research Centre and served as Curator of the Anup Sanskrit Library (attested 1946).
K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under M. A. Mehendale. She was later affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru University in 1983.

K. Munirathnam is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under N. S. Ramachandra Murthy. He served as Director (Epigraphy) I/c at the Archaeological Survey of India, attested between 2013 and 2018.

K. N. Jayatilleke was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under O. H. de A. Wijesekera and Ludwig Wittgenstein at Cambridge. He later served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon from circa 1951 to 1963.

K. N. Neelakantan Elayath is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as Assistant Professor at Government Arts College (1967–1969) and Sree Krishna College (1972–1984), and as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calicut (1990–2003).
